purpose: Turn the product-grade sandbox workbench prototype into a formalization-readiness pilot pack.

surfaces.title: First Run Script
answers: How do I try this in five minutes?

surfaces.title: Daily Operator Flow
answers: What do I do when a new item appears?

surfaces.title: Receipt Inspector
answers: Which verifier, hash, or report should I inspect?

surfaces.title: Triage and Dirty-State Panel
answers: What is blocked, stale, dirty, missing an anchor, review due, or action risky?

surfaces.title: Formalization Decision Matrix
answers: Which route should a real Obsidian workbench take?
surfaces.boundary: decision matrix is not a merge approval

surfaces.title: Acceptance Gates
answers: What must pass before a user can trust the workflow?
surfaces.boundary: gate pass is not mainline approval

surfaces.title: Reviewer Packet
surfaces.boundary: reviewer pass is not Product Acceptance

surfaces.title: Failure Messages
answers: Why was this blocked and what is the safe alternative?
surfaces.boundary: block reason is not a truth judgment

surfaces.title: Formalization Readiness Packet
answers: What would a later approved formalization slice need to touch?
surfaces.boundary: readiness packet is not permission to execute

surfaces.title: Rollout Backlog
answers: What is next after this sandbox?
surfaces.boundary: backlog item is not approval to execute

journeys.goal: A new operator can understand the workbench without reading architecture first.
journeys.expected_answer: This is a sandbox pilot pack, not the formal vault.
journeys.boundary_check: contains sandbox only and no formal vault write
journeys.stop_condition: Stop if any step asks for sync, commit, push, install, or formal vault write.

journeys.goal: An operator can decide where a new candidate belongs.
journeys.expected_answer: Triage can route work, but cannot approve truth or action basis.
journeys.stop_condition: Stop if routing is presented as reviewed knowledge.

journeys.goal: An operator can find the verification trail for a slice.
journeys.stop_condition: Stop if a receipt is described as source support.

journeys.goal: A product owner can compare formalization routes without accidental merge.
steps: Select a recommended next sandbox route
journeys.expected_answer: Recommended route still requires separate user approval.
journeys.boundary_check: decision matrix is not a merge approval
journeys.stop_condition: Stop if the matrix authorizes Obsidian sync or mainline promotion.

journeys.goal: A reviewer can tell whether the pilot pack is ready for the next slice.
journeys.expected_answer: Only GPT-5.5 xhigh Product Acceptance can pass product grade.
journeys.boundary_check: validator pass is not Product Acceptance
journeys.stop_condition: Stop if validator output is treated as reviewer approval.

decision_options.label: Keep static HTML cockpit as inspection surface
decision_options.fit: Best for fast review and browser smoke tests.
decision_options.risk: Can feel outside native Obsidian if used alone.

decision_options.label: Translate to Obsidian-native Markdown and Bases
decision_options.fit: Best native operator experience after explicit formal-vault approval.
decision_options.risk: Would write formal vault and possibly .base files, so it is not allowed in this slice.

decision_options.label: Build a local read-only sidecar
decision_options.fit: Best for search, validation, and cockpit refresh without mutating the vault.
decision_options.risk: Could drift into a runtime service if not tightly scoped.

decision_options.label: Hybrid: native Markdown entry plus static inspector plus read-only validator
decision_options.fit: Best next product route because it keeps Obsidian feel and auditability separate.
decision_options.risk: Needs a later approved slice to touch the formal vault.

acceptance_gates.test: A new operator reaches the boundary FAQ and first run checklist in three links or fewer.
Status, blocker, receipt, and next safe step are visible from Pilot Home.
P2-21 verification, boundary, reviewer, and product reports are linked from the pilot pack.
No page says sandbox pass equals reviewed knowledge, evidence support, action basis, merge, sync, commit, or push.
All generated files stay under this slice path.
Reviewer, Boundary Auditor, and GPT-5.5 xhigh Product Acceptance reports exist before next slice.
